notes: Summary: Mid-market CX SaaS (B2B) evaluating hosted API now moving toward Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation.
Hosted trial: 3-week free credits trial (Jan 28 - Feb 18) using hosted_api. Ran support chat + document search flows and an embeddings pipeline for semantic search.

Traffic snapshot during trial: avg QPS 6 (mixed: conversational + embeddings backfills), peak QPS 22 during US business hours, median concurrency observed 35 concurrent requests (spiky, 11:30-13:30 PST).

Token mix observed: ~62% generation (avg prompt 120 tokens / avg completion 240 tokens), 28% embeddings (avg 512-dim requests, mostly short inputs), 10% reranking calls (short generation with higher compute per call). Monthly extrapolation from trial: ~120M tokens/month if they convert 1:1 to production for current feature set.
Latency & SLO: product team targets p95 < 350ms for simple support-turn responses and p95 < 700ms for longer doc-summaries. Current hosted trial p95 ~ 420ms for gen; embeddings p95 ~ 180ms.
Cost sensitivity: medium. Willing to commit to reserved capacity for 20-40% discount vs hosted on sustained workloads, but requires clear sizing + predictable unit economics.

Model preferences: prefer smaller LR/fast variants for chat (Llama-2-7B and optimized 13B variants tested), heavier model for summarization only. Interested in Redwood's verified model catalog and quantization recommendations.
Routing/fallback: Request ability to route low-latency chat to smaller model; fallback to multi-region capacity during peak; want automatic fallback policies documented.

Security & compliance: must pass SSO/SAML integration, SOC2 audit evidence, KMS integration for key management, and EU data residency assurances for GDPR customers. Air-gapped not required today but VPC + private control plane is needed.

Hosted trial learnings: batching + prefix caching reduced observed token cost by ~18% on chat flows. However, KV cache hit rate varied between 40-65% depending on prompt patterns — ops wants tuning suggestions from Optimize.

Dedicated sizing ask: Silkshore asked for capacity plan covering baseline vs 99th percentile traffic for QPS and concurrency, recommended GPU types (A10G vs A100), expected concurrency per GPU given their token distribution, and guidance on autoscale/burst policies.

Preliminary sizing notes from SE: For their mix (median request ~360 tokens total), estimate ~1.8k tokens/sec sustained -> translate to ~300 QPS of small-chat-equivalents. With batching and quantized 8-bit kernels, 4x concurrency per GPU expected for chat model variants. Recommended starting pool: 4x A10G (can be scaled) or 1-2x A100 for heavy summarization tasks. Need traffic traces to refine numbers.

POC ask: 2-week Dedicated canary (single customer namespace) with traffic mirroring from hosted to validate latency/cost and to exercise autoscaling policies. They want per-token billing visibility and per-route dashboards in Redwood Console.

Commercials: asked for an example contract with monthly reserved slots and burst capacity pricing. Finance wants ARR estimate and a 60-day trial clause. Forecasted ARR if they commit: $120k-180k first-year (conservative).
Quotes from the CTO: 'We need predictable tail latency under production load — if Redwood can show consistent p95 under our load and clear cost math, we can sign reserved capacity.'

Next steps captured in CRM: 1) SE sizing workshop (2/hrs) scheduled 2026-03-12 (held), 2) Customer to share anonymized traces + sample token histogram, 3) Redwood to deliver Dedicated sizing doc + pricing by 2026-03-17, 4) Align legal & procurement timelines for April close.
Open questions: exact GPU SKU preference (cloud pricing sensitivity), whether embeddings heavy backfills should run on separate pool, SLA latency targets for EU customers during regional failover.
